_comment: Per-platform completion levers for the full /implement run (v4.13.2). One row per integration key registered in scripts/lib/integrations/__init__.py, plus surface rows for surfaces that share an integration (owner names the registering integration). Each lever is VERIFIED (first-party vendor URL fetched on the verified date) or 'none documented'. The completion gate reads continuation.format; run-plan lists rows whose headless lever is VERIFIED but hard-codes its own launch flags and never reads them from here. Validated by tests/validators/test_completion_levers.py. Human companion: completion-levers.md. Re-verify a row before relying on it; vendor pages move.

native_goal.summary: Modes are code/ask/architect/help only.

headless.launch: aider --message "<prompt>" (-m/--msg) or --message-file/-f; process reply then exit

aider.notes: No hook system documented in the options reference.

native_goal.summary: No page fetched that scopes /goal to Antigravity 1.0.

antigravity.notes: https://antigravity.google/docs/hooks/ says hooks work across "Antigravity 2.0, Antigravity CLI, and Antigravity IDE"; it is not stated whether "Antigravity IDE" means the 1.0 product. Needs a manual check before claiming coverage for 1.0.

native_goal.summary: /goal instructs the agent to work continuously until the objective is fully achieved (runs builds, diagnoses errors, applies edits without turn-by-turn confirmation). Listed under Reasoning, All plans, across Antigravity 2.0 (Desktop & Web) and Antigravity CLI. No preview gate stated.

continuation.vendor_shape: JSON {"decision": "continue", "reason": "..."} prevents stopping and re-enters the loop

prompt_submit.event: Only five events documented: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreInvocation, PostInvocation, Stop. PreInvocation (before model call) is the nearest, but it is not a prompt-submit event.

antigravity2.notes: Desktop app; headless entry lives on the CLI row.

native_goal.summary: Same /goal as Antigravity 2.0; slash-commands page lists it for Antigravity CLI.
native_goal.headless_entry: Not documented whether agy -p "/goal ..." runs the goal loop.

headless.resume: agy -c / agy --continue (workspace-scoped most recent), agy --resume <id>; combination with -p not stated

native_goal.summary: /goal <condition> sets a session-scoped completion condition; after each turn a small fast model (Haiku default) judges met / not yet met / impossible and starts another turn if not met. Implemented as a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook. Unavailable when disableAllHooks is true, allowManagedHooksOnly is set, or the workspace is untrusted. Stops the loop after several no-tool-use turns in a row. Condition up to 4,000 chars.
native_goal.headless_entry: claude -p "/goal <condition>" (runs the loop to completion in one invocation; add --output-format stream-json --verbose to see progress). Goal is restored on --continue / --resume.

continuation.cap: Claude Code overrides a Stop hook after it blocks eight times in a row without progress; raise with CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP.
continuation.vendor_shape: Top-level JSON on stdout {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."}; or exit code 2 (reason from JSON reason if present, else stderr). Input carries stop_hook_active.

claude.notes: A first WebFetch summary of /docs/en/hooks claimed Stop decision is nested in hookSpecificOutput; the hooks guide states verbatim that PostToolUse and Stop use a top-level decision: "block". Top-level is the documented form.

native_goal.summary: /goal keeps Codex working across turns toward a verifiable stopping condition; goal states active / paused / complete / budget-limited. Gated behind feature flag: [features] goals = true in config.toml, or `codex features enable goals`.

continuation.config: ~/.codex/hooks.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, <repo>/.codex/hooks.json, <repo>/.codex/config.toml, plugin hooks/hooks.json. Hooks enabled by default ([features] hooks = false disables).
continuation.vendor_shape: Top-level JSON {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."}; Codex continues and uses reason as the new continuation prompt. Or exit code 2 with the reason on stderr. Input carries stop_hook_active.

headless.resume: codex exec resume --last "<prompt>" | codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>

codex.notes: developers.openai.com/codex/* now 308-redirects to learn.chatgpt.com. Docs do not say whether /goal works under codex exec; no continuation cap documented.

native_goal.summary: Umbrella row: see copilot/cli (/goal + autopilot) and copilot/vscode (Autopilot agent mode).

continuation.vendor_shape: CLI: top-level decision block; VS Code: nested hookSpecificOutput

copilot.notes: Formats differ per surface; never treat the umbrella row as a single contract.

native_goal.summary: /goal starts or refocuses autopilot mode, optionally with an explicit objective (e.g. /goal Refactor the auth module); /goal on and /goal off toggle; --max-ai-credits caps spend. Autopilot works until it determines the task is complete; by default pauses after 5 continuation messages (--max-autopilot-continues adjusts).

continuation.config: .github/hooks/*.json, ~/.copilot/hooks/ ($COPILOT_HOME/hooks/), inline hooks in .github/copilot/settings(.local).json or ~/.copilot/settings.json, policy dirs, plugins
continuation.cap: After 8 consecutive block continuations the system overrides the hook.
continuation.vendor_shape: Top-level JSON {"decision": "block", "reason": "..."}; decision forces another agent turn using reason as the prompt. Exit code 2 is only a warning (stderr surfaced, processing continues), NOT a block.

copilot/cli.notes: Autopilot page itself does not mention /goal; /goal is documented in the CLI command reference. Autopilot non-interactive example from https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/autopilot.

native_goal.summary: Autopilot is an agent mode (mode picker) that lets the agent work autonomously until it determines the task is complete; auto-approves all tools and retries on errors. Advanced Autopilot (Preview, setting chat.autopilot.advanced.enabled = true) delegates the completion decision to a small fast model after each turn.

continuation.config: .github/hooks/*.json (workspace), ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json (user); .claude/settings(.local).json and ~/.claude/settings.json only with chat.useClaudeHooks (off by default); chat.hookFilesLocations adds/disables locations. Hooks experience is in Preview.
continuation.cap: none documented (docs only advise checking stop_hook_active)
continuation.vendor_shape: Nested: {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "Stop", "decision": "block", "reason": "..."}}; reason required when blocking. Input carries stop_hook_active.

native_goal.summary: /goal tracks a durable goal with an active or paused status line, continues across idle and headless runs, pauses on Ctrl+C. CLI changelog (2026-08-11): "This is rolling out and gated." Also in the 2026-08-19 cloud agents changelog.
native_goal.headless_entry: Changelog says the goal continues across headless runs; exact `agent -p "/goal ..."` syntax not documented.

continuation.vendor_shape: {"decision": "deny", "reason": "..."} rejects the response and forces a retry; reason is sent to the agent as a new prompt. Exit code 2 also retries using stderr as the feedback prompt. Optional hookSpecificOutput.clearContext.

gemini-cli.notes: A search-result snippet claimed AfterAgent ignores flow control; the fetched reference page contradicts it (only SessionEnd and PreCompress ignore flow control). Product is enterprise-only after 2026-06-18 per repo roster.

native_goal.summary: /goal sets a standing goal; a judge model checks after each turn and Hermes auto-continues until done, paused/cleared, or the turn budget (goals.max_turns, default 20) is hit, then auto-pauses. User messages preempt.

continuation.config: Python plugin via ctx.register_hook(), or shell hook in profile config.yaml hooks: block
continuation.cap: agent.max_verify_nudges, default 3 consecutive continues per turn (built-in + pre_verify)
continuation.vendor_shape: Return {"action": "continue", "message": "..."}; message appended as a synthetic user turn and the loop runs again. Fires ONLY when the agent edited code this turn and a pre_verify hook is registered.

prompt_submit.event: pre_llm_call (once per turn before the tool loop; nearest equivalent)

hermes.notes: Goals docs are silent on one-shot runs: the lead 'not in one-shot' is neither confirmed nor refuted. The pre_verify code-edit gate means it is not a general turn-end continuation hook.

native_goal.summary: /goal starts goal mode: a persistent objective worked toward across automatically continuing turns, with completion checked each cycle. In manual permission mode it may pause for tool approvals.
native_goal.headless_entry: kimi -p "/goal ..." (prompt mode supports only goal creation); exit codes 0 = completed, 3 = blocked, 6 = paused

continuation.vendor_shape: Exit code 2 blocks; stderr is the reason. For Stop, if blocked a message can be appended to let the model continue the turn. JSON form documented is hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision "deny" (general blocking shape).

headless.resume: kimi --continue / -c (most recent in cwd) | --session / -S <id>; mutually exclusive

kimi.notes: Whether the JSON deny shape (vs exit 2) continues a Stop was not stated precisely; exit 2 is the safe documented path.

native_goal.summary: README describes "Auto mode - End-to-end tool-using sessions with verification gates and git checkpoints"; no condition-until-met goal command is stated.

nexus-ai.notes: README only, per scope. It mentions headless and scheduled agent runs with an Ask inbox, but no CLI flags or resume. Auto mode may qualify as a goal lever; the maintainer should confirm from the Nexus-AI source.

native_goal.summary: /goal is session state, not a loop: a shared target that moves with the session key and survives restarts, explicitly not a background task/task queue. Model tools get_goal/create_goal/update_goal. Requires the built-in OpenClaw runtime; unavailable for native Codex and external runtimes.

continuation.config: Plugin register(api) with api.on('before_agent_finalize', handler); TypeScript
continuation.cap: maxAttempts defaults to one extra pass per key; the embedded runner allows at most three revisions overall; 15 s handler budget
continuation.vendor_shape: Return {action: "revise", reason} for one more model pass (optional retry {instruction, idempotencyKey?, maxAttempts?}); {action: "finalize"} overrides. Not run on user abort.

headless.launch: openclaw agent --message "<text>" (or --message-file) with a session selector; `agent exec` recommended for CI

continuation.vendor_shape: No return value refuses the stop. A plugin can observe event.type === 'session.idle' and call client.session.prompt({path:{id}, body:{parts:[{type:'text', text:'...'}]}}) to start a new turn. The docs do not show this continuation pattern explicitly; it is composed from two documented primitives.

prompt_submit.event: Plugin docs list only message.* events (message.updated etc.); no chat.message/prompt-submit event named.

opencode.notes: session.prompt documented at https://opencode.ai/docs/sdk/. Treat continuation as a composed pattern, weaker evidence than a documented refuse-stop contract.
